title: The curse of King Tut's tomb

slides.text: HE OPENED KING TUT'S TOMB. 5 MONTHS LATER HE WAS DEAD.
Valley of the Kings, Egypt. November 1922. Howard Carter's team finds a staircase cut into the rock.
At the bottom: a sealed door. The tomb of the boy king Tutankhamun, untouched for over 3,000 years.
Asked if he could see anything inside, Carter answered: 'Yes, wonderful things.'
The dig was paid for by Lord Carnarvon, a rich English earl. He was right there when the tomb was opened.
Over the next ten years they carried out more than 5,000 objects. Gold. Chariots. A golden mask.
April 1923. Carnarvon dies in Cairo. Blood poisoning, from an infected mosquito bite.
The legend says the lights of Cairo went out the moment he died... and his dog back in England howled and dropped dead.
Newspapers went wild with 'the curse of the pharaohs.' Every death tied to the tomb made headlines.
But Howard Carter lived another 16 years. Scientists found no sign of a curse. Tut's treasures are still on display today.
